stories.headline: Houthi forces capture Yemeni port city of Mokha as crude oil prices surge past $100
stories.body:
Houthi forces captured the Yemeni port city of Mokha from Saudi-backed forces. The port city sits about 80 kilometers, or 50 miles, from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Pro-government commander Tarek Salah said his forces moved their command center on the west coast to a safe location. A Yemeni military source told AFP that Houthi forces were pushing towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait. Fighting started again in Yemen as Houthi forces moved south towards the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

A Yemeni military source told AFP that Houthi fighters also captured Zuqar Island in the Red Sea. They took the island after rocket barrages and a boat assault. Houthi spokesman Yahya Sarea said Saudi warplanes carried out 64 air strikes across four western Yemeni provinces within 24 hours. Saudi authorities reported that Houthi missile and drone strikes on September 8 injured 73 civilians. They said the strikes also temporarily stopped operations at multiple oil facilities.

The fighting caused global oil prices to jump sharply. The benchmark US oil contract West Texas Intermediate rose above $100 a barrel on September 10 after Houthis seized Mocha. Brent crude rose more than 6 percent past $107 a barrel on September 10. That was its highest level since May. Rystad Energy analyst Jorge Leon said oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz dropped. It fell from around 8 million barrels per day in late August to between 1.5 million and 2 million barrels per day.

Financial markets reacted to the news as well. The 30-year US Treasury bond yield reached 5.36 percent. This marked a new peak since 2007. US producer price inflation climbed to 5.4 percent in August. That was up from 4.8 percent in July. The European Central Bank increased its benchmark interest rate to 2.5 percent on September 10.

stories.headline: Cargo ship fire at Qingdao port in China kills 25 people
stories.body:
Chinese state media CCTV reported 25 people died in a fire on a foreign-flagged cargo ship in Qingdao, China. At least 25 people were killed after a fire broke out aboard a ship at a shipyard in China. Five people remain missing after the cargo vessel fire at the shipyard in Qingdao.

There were 42 people on board the vessel. Seventeen people were evacuated from the ship. Five people were hospitalized in stable condition.

The ship involved in the fire was named the Ocean Melody. It is a 190-meter Liberia-flagged carrier that arrived in Qingdao on August 31. The fire began around 11:15 local time during maintenance work. Firefighters put out the blaze just over three hours later.

Chinese President Xi Jinping told authorities to thoroughly investigate fire hazards. President Xi instructed officials to strictly hold responsible parties to account. A shipyard explosion in Fujian province in August killed a rescue worker and injured 12 people.

stories.headline: Republicans hold midterm convention in Dallas as Donald Trump proposes $5,000 checks
stories.body:
Republican National Committee chair Joe Gruters opened the second night of the party's midterm convention in Dallas. The event marked the one-year anniversary of Charlie Kirk's death. Republicans gathered in Dallas to close their midterm convention before upcoming elections.

House Speaker Mike Johnson warned delegates that swing-seat Democrats vote with socialists. Johnson said communists will be in Congress next year. Donald Trump told CBS News he does not believe Congress needs to approve proposed $5,000 checks for Americans. Distributing $5,000 checks to all 276.8 million American adults would cost about $1.384 trillion.

The US government collected a record $195 billion in customs duties during fiscal year 2025. The US has brought in about $475 billion in tariff and excise tax revenue since early 2025. Over $100 billion was refunded after Supreme Court rulings.

Prosecutor Joe diGenova resigned from leading a Justice Department inquiry. The inquiry targeted former government officials who investigated Donald Trump. Democratic Senator John Fetterman made a surprise virtual address at the convention. Fetterman praised Republican Senator Dave McCormick. Pennsylvania state Representative Malcolm Kenyatta criticized Fetterman. Kenyatta called Fetterman the laziest Benedict Arnold America has seen and called on him to resign.

stories.headline: August 2026 recorded as joint-hottest month globally as El Nino grows
stories.body:
The Copernicus Climate Change Service reported August 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally. It tied with July 2023. August 2026 was 1.65 degrees Celsius warmer than the estimated 1850-1900 pre-industrial baseline.

Europe's climate monitor reported an unprecedented El Nino pattern is continuing to grow globally. Daily global extra-polar sea surface temperature reached a record high of 21.11 degrees Celsius in August 2026. Major European rivers experienced exceptionally low flows during August. These rivers included the Rhine, Danube, Southern Bug, and Dnieper.

India recorded a mean monthly temperature of 28.01 degrees Celsius in August 2026. This made it the country's warmest August since 1901.

In the contiguous US, June through August 2026 averaged 74.37 degrees Fahrenheit, or 23.54 degrees Celsius. This broke the 1936 Dust Bowl record by nearly 0.4 degrees Fahrenheit.

stories.headline: School fire in eastern DR Congo leaves at least 24 children dead
stories.body:
Twenty-four schoolchildren died during a stampede while fleeing a fire at two schools in Bukavu in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Authorities confirmed at least 14 schoolchildren were killed in the fire that swept through the schools. A hospital in Bukavu admitted over 50 students from the fire, 14 of whom died. South Kivu Vice Governor Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge reported 19 girls and five boys were killed. Vice Governor Bwenge added that 29 people were injured.

The fire destroyed about 300 houses in Bukavu's Kadutu commune. M23 rebels previously captured the South Kivu provincial capital of Bukavu in February 2025.

stories.headline: BRICS Summit begins in New Delhi as Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping arrive
stories.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin landed in New Delhi on Friday to attend the BRICS summit. He arrived for a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The BRICS Summit 2026 marks Putin's first overseas participation in a BRICS summit since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. PM Modi and President Putin previously met in Bishkek on August 31 on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit.

The 18th BRICS summit is taking place at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi from September 12-13. Its theme is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.

Many global leaders are expected to attend the BRICS summit in New Delhi. Expected guests include Chinese President Xi Jinping, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to attend. This marks his first visit to India since taking office after President Ebrahim Raisi died in a helicopter crash in 2024. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, WHO head Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, and WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala are also attending. But Bangladesh will not be represented at the summit. Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir confirmed this despite an invitation sent to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

India and Russia are expanding economic and defense discussions. Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia and India are exploring cooperation in rare earths. Peskov said Russia is exploring the possible sale of Sukhoi Su-57 stealth fighter jets to India. Union Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu confirmed expanded talks on manufacturing aircraft in India. These include the IL-114 turboprop and Sukhoi Superjet 100. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said India and Russia aim to reach $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030. Goyal said the countries also target $50 billion in two-way investment by 2030. Bilateral trade between India and Russia currently stands at around $60 billion.

Delhi authorities put strict security measures in place. Special airspace restrictions apply from September 11 to September 13 within 300 kilometers of New Delhi. Safdarjung Airport will remain closed, except for specified military and police helicopter operations. Aircraft climbing near the restricted zone must reach around 29,000 feet by the time they are 200 kilometers from the capital. Normal scheduled commercial flights at Delhi's main airport will continue taking off and landing. Nearly 4,800 traffic personnel are deployed in Delhi for security and traffic management.

stories.headline: Delhi authorities seal Chandni Chowk shops following fatal Satya Niketan building collapse
stories.body:
Municipal workers sealed 56 jewellery and bullion shops in Chandni Chowk's Kucha Mahajani on Thursday. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi enforcement drive was intensified after a building collapse in Satya Niketan on September 6 left seven people dead. The five-storey paying guest building collapsed, killing seven people and injuring 12. Five of the seven people killed were Delhi University students.

Initial findings revealed the 50-year-old building in Satya Niketan had five floors despite only two floors being permitted. Police arrested the building owner, his son, the operator, and a contractor. Operator Shubham Tyagi was denied anticipatory bail by a Delhi court.

The Municipal Corporation of Delhi suspended five municipal officials over alleged negligence. Three additional engineers were suspended for negligence after the collapse. The All India Bullion and Jewellers Association questioned whether only traders will bear the brunt or if action will also be taken against government departments and politicians.

A Supreme Court Bench directed authorities across India to file affidavits on compliance regarding unauthorized constructions. Amicus curiae Ajit Kumar Sinha brought the Satya Niketan collapse to the Supreme Court's attention. The Delhi High Court scheduled further hearings on public interest litigation for September 25.
